Dear Community,

@Guoxiong Gao, @Haocheng Ju and I are excited to announce the official launch of

LeanSearch (https://leansearch.net/),

a powerful semantic search engine for mathlib, developed by the AI4Math team at BICMR@PKU. It's now available for everyone to use! :tada:

LeanSearch is designed to help you find theorems, definitions, instances, and more within Mathlib. It supports both natural language and formal language queries. One of its standout features is its great performance when dealing with theorem names and formulas. We invite you to experience its capabilities firsthand by trying queries such as "Schroeder-Bernstein theorem" or "$\pi > 3$". Additionally, when you do not find a specific theorem and need a little extra help, LeanSearch offers a "Query augmentation" feature. It enhances your original query with a more detailed, LLM-generated version, ensuring you get the most relevant results. More introduction can be found in this video:
LeanSearch.MP4

Please be aware that the current version of LeanSearch does not support image-based searches. Additionally, there may be slight variations in search results compared to the video demonstration.

As LeanSearch is currently in its beta phase, we are eager to gather your feedback to enhance the user experience. We have created a dedicated thread for discussions and feedback. Please note that service may be temporarily interrupted during updates to our search engine.

For those interested in the technical aspects of LeanSearch, here is a preprint paper detailing its methodologies.

We look forward to your engagement and contributions as we continue to refine and expand the capabilities of LeanSearch!

We are excited to announce a major update to LeanSearch at leansearch.net!

In this release, we've introduced several major enhancements:

  1. A fresh new UI design featuring a card-like display mode, inspired by the Mathlib4 documentation.
  2. LeanSearch now supports searches across all types of items, not just theorems.
  3. An easy-to-use API is now available for everyone! Check out the details at LeanSearchDocs.

In addition to these major updates, we've made several improvements for better user experiences:

  1. We've merged informal and formal search capabilities by enhancing the lexical matching ability of our semantic embedding engine. Future updates will further refine this capability.
  2. The documentation link has been moved to a "Go to doc" button for improved visibility.
  3. We've added "thumbs up" and "thumbs down" icons to each item, which store the feedback and help us to improve the system.
  4. Results in both formal and informal statements are now rendered more clearly.
  5. The search engine has been accelerated for a smoother experience.
  6. A copy button is now available to directly copy the formal name of items.
  7. A caption has been added to encourage users to use query augmentation to enhance retrieval.
  8. The GUI is now better optimized for mobile devices.

In our upcoming update, we plan to integrate a more up-to-date database (such as Mathlib4 v4.11.0), further enhance our lexical matching capabilities, and improve the GUI. We warmly welcome your suggestions!

Acknowledgements:

LeanSearch was developed with contributions from Guoxiong Gao, Haocheng Ju, Jiedong Jiang, Zihan Qin, Qi Gao, Zixun Guo, Tianyi Xu, Kelan Liu, and Anjie Dong, under the supervision of Dr. Bin Dong.

Finally, we want to express our gratitude to everyone who has kindly advised us throughout the development of LeanSearch. Your support has been invaluable.
